title: Readers could not reliably distinguish AI short stories from human ones
friendlyTitle: Most readers could not tell AI and human short stories apart
summary: Across three experiments involving more than 2,500 participants, researchers found that readers performed at chance when identifying roughly 1,000-word ChatGPT and human-written stories. AI stories received higher average quality and immersion ratings, but either kind of story was rated lower when readers were told AI wrote it.
friendlySummary: In three tests, more than 2,500 people read short stories made by ChatGPT or people. They usually could not tell who wrote them, and they gave lower scores when they believed AI was the writer.
whyItMatters: For short-form writing, audience response may depend as much on disclosure and expectations as on the text itself. Writers and publishers should separate readability from literary quality, disclose AI involvement clearly and avoid assuming readers can identify synthetic work unaided.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A smooth story is not always a great story, and people’s feelings about AI affect their judgment. Clear labels and honest editing are important when AI helps with writing.
